strengths: Clear identification and motivation of the collapse problem in test-time entropy minimization with compelling evidence
Simple, elegant solution requiring no augmentations or extra encoder passes with negligible computational overhead

Comprehensive empirical evaluation across diverse architectures (ResNet50-GN, ViT variants, ConvNeXt-Tiny, Swin-Tiny), tasks (vision and language), and challenging test scenarios (label shifts: 52.9% vs 38.8%, blind-spot: 52.0% vs 29.8%)
Extensive ablation studies (Tables 4, 8-10) providing useful insights on design choices and robustness
Good empirical analysis showing the method regularizes biased signals beyond just preventing collapse
Works across different model architectures and generalizes well to challenging scenarios with incorrect pseudo-labels
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: directly applies existing SimSiam asymmetric design to entropy minimization rather than proposing fundamentally new techniques

Weak theoretical analysis: Theorem 1 Part (1) analyzed under α=0 (eliminating regularization), doesn't provide deep insight into why the specific design is optimal, lacks comparison with simpler alternatives
Insufficient justification of design choices: why linear predictors suffice, why symmetric KL divergence, why align to stop-gradient target specifically, what makes good predictors for this task
Experimental rigor concerns: no error bars or confidence intervals, varying learning rates across models (Table C.2), no statistical significance testing, artificial stress test scenarios

Incomplete failure analysis: method succeeds in only 4/7 domains for collapsed model recovery (E.3) with no systematic analysis; no comparison with simpler collapse-prevention baselines (entropy+threshold, entropy+regularization)
Table 9 shows ZeroSiam+EATA/DeYO doesn't consistently beat standalone ZeroSiam, suggesting limited generalizability with other methods

strengths: Addresses a real and practically important problem: model collapse during test-time entropy minimization, with clear empirical demonstration (Figure 2)
Elegant and practical solution with minimal overhead: single linear predictor + stop-gradient, no augmentations or extra encoder passes, same runtime as Tent (Table 1)

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: multiple models (ResNet50-GN, ViT variants, ConvNeXt-Tiny, Swin-Tiny, Llama3.1-8B), diverse test scenarios (label shifts, batch size=1, blind-spot adaptation, noise resistance), both vision and language domains
Extends beyond collapse prevention: demonstrates improved generalization even without visible collapse through adaptive bias signal filtration (Section 3.2, Figure 2)
Provides theoretical grounding via Theorem 1 showing online branch exhibits stronger collapse tendency and alignment term suppresses collapse-inducing gradients, with convergence guarantees
Strong reproducibility: detailed implementation details, public models/datasets, supplementary ablations (Tables 8-10), statistical analysis with 5 random seeds (Table I)
weaknesses: Limited architectural novelty: core asymmetry mechanism (predictor + stop-gradient) directly borrowed from SimSiam; main contribution is application to entropy minimization rather than methodological innovation

Theoretical analysis has significant gaps: Assumptions 1-2 are strong and unverified; Theorem 1 conclusions are loose (e.g., existence of h_min without guidance on equilibrium quality); bounds depend on uncharacterized Lipschitz constants that likely vary across models

Hyperparameter sensitivity contradicts practicality claims: Table C.2 shows different (ηf, ηh) for each model; Figure 4 shows ~20% accuracy swings from learning rate changes; data-free ηh selection (E.6) only works for ResNet50-GN; claims of 'practical and easy to use' are overstated

Incomplete mechanistic understanding: paper asserts predictor 'absorbs shortcuts' (Observation 1) without rigorously explaining why Frobenius distance correlates with imbalance or how a linear FC layer specifically targets entropy-related shortcuts

Experimental design concerns: different hyperparameters per model complicate fair comparison; blind-spot evaluation is somewhat artificial (in practice, pre-knowing misclassified samples is unrealistic); pre-adaptation to pure Gaussian noise is an extreme scenario

Limited failure mode analysis: collapse recovery succeeds in only 4/7 domains with no explanation; integration with prior methods (Table 9) shows minimal synergy; notably weaker performance on Swin-Tiny unexplained

Narrow scope: evaluated only on image classification and language reasoning; unclear how well the 'shortcuts' concept generalizes to detection, segmentation, or other objectives beyond entropy minimization
